title: The churches of God shine like lights
source_text: Ὁ μὲν οὖν κατὰ τὸν Κέλσον Ἀπόλλων βούλεται τοὺς Μεταποντίνους ἐν θεῶν μοίρᾳ νέμειν τὸν Ἀριστέαν. ἐπεὶ δὲ οἱ Μεταποντῖνοι τὴν περὶ τοῦ Ἀριστέου ἀνθρώπου καὶ τάχα οὐ σπουδαίου ἐνάργειαν κρείττονα ἐνόμιζον εἶναι τοῦ περὶ αὐτοῦ χρησμοῦ ὡς θεοῦ ἢ θείων τιμῶν ἀξίου, διὰ τοῦτο οὐκ ἐβούλοντο πείθεσθαι τῷ Ἀπόλλωνι, καὶ οὕτως τὸν Ἀριστέαν οὐδεὶς νομίζει θεόν. περὶ δὲ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ εἴποιμεν ἂν, ἐπεὶ συμφέρον ἦν τῷ τῶν ἀνθρώπων γένει παραδέξασθαι αὐτὸν ὡς υἱὸν θεοῦ, θεὸν ἐληλυθότα ἐν ἀνθρωπίνῃ ψυχῇ καὶ σώματι, καὶ οὐκ ἐδόκει τοῦτο τῇ λιχνείᾳ τῶν φιλοσωμάτων δαιμόνων καὶ τῶν νομιζόντων αὐτοὺς θεοὺς εἶναι λυσιτελὲς, διὰ τοῦθ᾿ οἱ μὲν ἐπὶ γῆς δαίμονες. παρὰ τοῖς μὴ παιδευθεῖσι περὶ δαιμόνων νομιζόμενοι εἶναι θεοὶ. ἀλλὰ καὶ οἱ θεραπεύοντες αὐτοὺς ἐβουλήθησαν κωλῦσαι τὴν νομὴν τῆς Ἰησοῦ διδασκαλίας· ἑώρων γὰρ τὰς λοιβὰς καὶ τὰς κνίσσας, ἐφ᾿ αἷς λίχνως ἥδοντο, καθαιρουμένας ἐκ τοῦ κρατεῖν τὰ Ἰησοῦ μαθήματα. ὁ δὲ πέμψας τὸν Ἰησοῦν θεὸς ἐκλύσας πᾶσαν τὴν τῶν δαιμόνων ἐπιβουλὴν ἐποίησε πανταχοῦ τῆς οἰκουμένης ὑπὲρ τῆς τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐπιστροφῆς καὶ διορθώσεως κρατῆσαι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον Ἰησοῦ καὶ γενέσθαι πανταχοῦ ἐκκλησίας ἀντιπολιτευομένας ἐκκλησίαις δεισιδαιμόνων καὶ ἀκολάστων καὶ ἀδίκων· τοιαῦτα γὰρ τὰ πανταχοῦ πολιτευόμενα ἐν ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις τῶν πόλεων πλήθη. αἱ δὲ τοῦ θεοῦ Χριστῷ μαθητευθεῖσαι ἐκκλησίαι, συνεξεταζόμεναι ταῖς ὧν παροικοῦσι δήμων ἐκκλησίαις, „ὡς φωστῆρές“ εἰσιν „ἐν κόσμῳ.“ τίς γὰρ οὐκ ἂν ὁμολογήσαι καὶ τοὺς χείρους τῶν ἀπὸ τῆς ἐκκλησίας καὶ συγκρίσει βελτιόνων ἐλάττους πολλῷ κρείττους τυγχάνειν τῶν ἐν τοῖς δήμοις ἐκκλησιῶν;
pass_a_gloss: Then the Apollo according to Celsus wishes the Metapontines to assign Aristeas in the portion of the gods. But since the Metapontines considered the evidence (ἐνάργεια) about Aristeas, a man and perhaps (τάχα) not a worthy one (σπουδαῖος), stronger (κρείττων) than the oracle about him as a god or worthy of divine honours (θεῖαι τιμαί), on account of this they did not wish to obey Apollo, and thus no one considers Aristeas a god. But about Jesus we would say that, since it was advantageous (συμφέρον) to the race of men to receive (παραδέχομαι) him as Son of God (υἱὸς θεοῦ), God come (ἔρχομαι) in a human soul and body, and this did not seem profitable (λυσιτελές) to the gluttony (λιχνεία) of the body-loving (φιλοσώματοι) demons and of those considering them to be gods, on account of this the demons upon earth, considered to be gods among those not instructed (παιδεύω) about demons, but also those serving (θεραπεύω) them, wished to hinder (κωλύω) the spread (νομή) of the teaching (διδασκαλία) of Jesus; for they saw the libations (λοιβαί) and savours (κνῖσαι), in which they gluttonously (λίχνως) delighted (ἥδομαι), being destroyed (καθαιρέω) from the teachings of Jesus prevailing (κρατέω). But the God who sent Jesus, having dissolved (ἐκλύω) all the plotting (ἐπιβουλή) of the demons, made the gospel (εὐαγγέλιον) of Jesus prevail everywhere in the world for the turning (ἐπιστροφή) and correction (διόρθωσις) of men, and churches (ἐκκλησίαι) to come into being everywhere, living as rival citizens (ἀντιπολιτεύομαι) to the assemblies (ἐκκλησίαι) of the superstitious (δεισιδαίμονες) and licentious (ἀκόλαστοι) and unjust (ἄδικοι); for such are the multitudes (πλήθη) everywhere acting as citizens (πολιτεύομαι) in the assemblies of the cities. But the churches of God, discipled (μαθητεύω) to Christ, examined together with (συνεξετάζω) the assemblies of the peoples (δῆμοι) among whom they sojourn (παροικέω), 'are as lights (φωστῆρες) in the world (κόσμος)'. For who would not confess that even the worse of those from the church and those lesser by comparison (σύγκρισις) with the better happen to be much better than the assemblies in the peoples?
pass_b_english: So Apollo, as Celsus tells it, wants the Metapontines to count Aristeas among the gods. But since the Metapontines thought the plain evidence about Aristeas, a man and perhaps not a good one, stronger than the oracle that called him a god or worthy of divine honours, they were not willing to obey Apollo; and so no one regards Aristeas as a god.

About Jesus we would say this. It was to the advantage of the human race to receive him as Son of God, God come in a human soul and body; and this did not seem profitable to the gluttony of the body-loving demons or of those who think them gods. For this reason the demons on earth, who are thought to be gods by those not instructed about demons, and also those who serve them, wanted to hinder the spread of the teaching of Jesus. For they saw that the libations and the savour of sacrifices, in which they greedily took pleasure, were being done away with as the teachings of Jesus prevailed. But God, who sent Jesus, brought to nothing all the plotting of the demons, and made the gospel of Jesus prevail in every part of the world for the conversion and amendment of human beings, and made churches arise everywhere that live as a rival commonwealth to the assemblies of the superstitious, the licentious and the unjust. For such are the crowds that everywhere act as citizens in the assemblies of the cities. But the churches of God that have been made disciples of Christ, when compared with the assemblies of the peoples among whom they dwell as sojourners, are "like lights in the world" (Philippians 2:15). For who would not admit that even the worse members of the church, and those who fall short by comparison with the better, are much better than the assemblies of the peoples?

choices.choice: Origen plays on ἐκκλησία, used both for the Christian church and for the civic assembly of a Greek city (the δῆμος in assembly). The reading text uses 'churches' for the Christian ἐκκλησίαι and 'assemblies' for the civic ones; English cannot keep the single word. ἀντιπολιτευομένας rendered 'living by a rival citizenship to'; παροικοῦσι rendered 'dwell as sojourners'. 'ὡς φωστῆρες ἐν κόσμῳ' quotes Philippians 2:15 (cited inline). 'Χριστῷ μαθητευθεῖσαι' rendered 'made disciples of Christ'. 'θεὸν ἐληλυθότα ἐν ἀνθρωπίνῃ ψυχῇ καὶ σώματι' kept exactly as 'God come in a human soul and body'. 'οἱ θεραπεύοντες αὐτούς' are the demons' worshippers (human), set beside the demons themselves. 'λοιβαί' and 'κνῖσαι' pick up the Homeric line quoted in chapter 28. The final comparison is with 'τῶν ἐν τοῖς δήμοις ἐκκλησιῶν', rendered 'the assemblies of the peoples'. The 'sending' of Jesus by God is a common Johannine idea but not a quotation here, so not cited. ἀντιπολιτευομένας now rendered 'live as a rival commonwealth to'; ἐπιστροφή rendered 'conversion'.
